newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanese 9-month exports up 28 pct - Banque Audi.
newsitem.headline: Lebanese 9-month exports up 28 pct - Banque Audi.

text.p: Lebanon's exports jumped 27.9 percent to $742 million in the first nine months of the year, Banque Audi said in its latest quarterly economic report.
Third quarter exports were $293 million, up 30.8 percent on the second quarter according to figures issued by the High Customs Council, the bank said.

"The production growth, in a context of a 9.6 percent decline in bank credits to industry, reveals an improvement in the competitiveness of domestic goods despite the continuous appreciation of the Lebanese pound," it said.
Banque Audi is one of Lebanon's leading commercial banks and the reports prepared by its economic analysis unit are well regarded in financial and business circles.

"With a 65 percent capacity utilisation ratio, the growth perspectives of the agricultural and industrial sectors are encouraging; yet they depend on an integrated industrial policy," the report said.
Agricultural exports were 10.2 percent of the total and reached $30 million in the third quarter, it said.
Bank credits to agriculture were $8 million in the third quarter and the total for the first nine months was $32 million compared with $35 million in the same period last year.
Bank credits to industry were $36 million in the third quarter and $143 million in the first nine months -- a decline of 9.6 percent on the same period last year.

However, imports of industrial machines doubled to $102 million in the third quarter and were $183 million for the first nine months, a 96.1 percent increase on the first nine months of 1995, the bank said.
This reflected the replenishment of capital assets and "extending industrial activities towards new high value-added products reflecting the comparative advantages of the Lebanese economy," it said.

Some 109 new factories were set up in the third quarter, creating 854 new jobs at an investment of 22 billion Lebanese pounds. This brought the total for the first three quarters to 345 new factories, 2,464 new jobs and 71 billion pounds in new investments.

This represented a progression of 10.9 percent in the establishment of new factories, 1.9 percent for creation of jobs and 0.9 percent for new investments compared with the first nine months of 1995, the report said.
The bulk of new investments went to the food and beverage industry and to minerals, chemicals, wood and furniture.
